label: M-02
title: Half of every annihilation's phUSD is minted against no incoming value, and the resulting liability is unbounded, unscheduled and unrecorded
fingerprintNote: sha256(contract:function:rootCauseClass)[:16] - legacy form, empty entryPoint. Carried verbatim from sanitized.json; reproduces from fingerprintBasis.

classification.assetImpact: Every annihilation mints `amount` phUSD (:236) against no incoming value. The resulting liability is unbounded (mint at :179 has no cap, schedule, or tie to yield or collateral), unscheduled, and recorded nowhere - no contract tracks unbacked phUSD supply. Each outstanding antimatter token is a permanent exercisable ~$1 call on the phUSD collateral pool. The loss is realised as peg dilution borne by phUSD holders and by whatever protocol-owned liquidity absorbs the annihilator's sell.
attackPath: 1. Receive N antimatter free as a staking reward (:180, approved-minter gated).
2. Acquire N (rescaled) stablecoin at ~$1 - REAL capital the actor must part with.
3. annihilateFrom(stable, self, self, N): burn N AM, surrender $N of stable, receive ~2N phUSD.

4. Sell 2N phUSD into protocol-owned liquidity at price p. Gross of the antimatter leg the flow is 2Np - N. NOT a standing profit claim: the antimatter consumed is itself worth ~max(0, 2p-1) per unit, so under market pricing arbitrage drives the round-trip return toward that value and the excess toward zero. The reportable core is the issuance structure (no cap, no budget, no liability view), not an arbitrage yield.
5. Recycle. 100% return per cycle at p = $1.00, permissionless, no flash loan - and it keeps paying arbitrageurs until phUSD reaches half peg.
classification.likelihood: Certain to be exercised once antimatter is emitted at volume - it is not an attack, it is the token's designed use, and it is rational for every holder. Currently gated by how much antimatter exists, which is an undecided policy variable.
classification.assumptions: antimatter is emitted in quantity; there is liquidity to sell 2N phUSD into. No minimum phUSD price is assumed - price affects only how an individual actor books the round trip, not the fact that the unbacked issuance is uncapped, unbudgeted and unmeasured.
classification.externalRequirements: An approved minter must actually emit antimatter (setApprovedMinter, :151). PARK-003 records that antimatter is NOT yet wired into phoenix-phase-2-staging, so emission policy is entirely undecided on-chain.

justification: MEDIUM for the CURRENT code, as filed - weighed against both an upgrade and a downgrade. Not HIGH: there is no atomic attack and no specific victim. Annihilation is one-way and the actor must actually hold antimatter and actually part with real stablecoin, so nothing is stolen in a transaction; the harm is diffuse dilution realised only through market sale. Crucially for the CURRENT tree, emission is owner-gated - only approved minters mint antimatter - so no permissionless drain exists today. Labelling this High now would be overstatement of a policy exposure, and overstatement is a pipeline-reject condition. Not LOW/QA: the liability is real, permanent, unbounded and completely unaccounted; it lands on parties who never consented; phUSD has NO redemption path anywhere (verified), which means this never surfaces as on-chain insolvency that some mechanism would catch - it surfaces only as peg pressure, with no on-chain control and not even an on-chain OBSERVATION of the exposure. An unmeasured unbounded liability is not a state-handling nit. C4 Medium - 'value leak with stated assumptions and external requirements' - fits exactly. INTENDED DESIGN IS NOT A DEFENCE (Law 1 over Law 2): specStatus is FAITHFUL-BUT-UNSAFE. The declared intent at :188-189 and in CLAUDE.md is implemented precisely; the intent itself is the hazard, so it is filed as a spec-level security finding and dual-channelled to spec-conformance as F-04. In-source NatSpec carries no suppression authority. Law-2 intent is UNGRADED, not passed: no storyDir and no [story-NNN] on any of the 6 commits (PARK-002). The standing Phoenix rule 'externally-derived yield over-payment is opportunity cost, not loss' was checked and does NOT apply - this is dilution of the phUSD collateral base, not over-payment of a reward budget.
recommendation: Treat Antimatter.totalSupply() as the protocol's unbacked-phUSD liability and expose it as such - at minimum a view reporting it next to phUSD.totalSupply().
Bound emission at the source: a supply cap or per-period mint budget on :179, so the liability cannot be enlarged by a single call from any approved minter.
If the intended policy is that emission is budgeted against realised protocol yield, enforce it on-chain - the code has no representation of that policy at all.
Correct the NatSpec at :18 (tracked separately as DEDUP-015).

evidence.invariantQuantification: invariant_04 PASSES as an EXACT equality over 76,800 calls in both decimal regimes: phUSD.totalSupply() minus stablecoin in custody (18dp-normalised) == cumulative antimatter burned. The pass is not an all-clear - it is the measurement that the uncollateralised leg is exactly 1:1 with antimatter burned, no rounding drift. invariant_05 separately confirms every stablecoin unit pulled reached strategy custody.
evidence.scopeLimit: invariants 04/05 pin exchangeRate at 1e18; rate divergence is DEDUP-005's territory.

sanitizer.reason: No known-issues document exists for this project (knownIssuesFile/Source null, knownIssues empty, verified at HEAD) so KI suppression has no authority; no C4 known-invalid class genuinely applies; not a malicious-owner vector; ledger empty so no prior entry to reconcile against.

additionalContext.econFaithMergeJustification: FAITH-002 and ECON-001 are the same defect at the same line (:236) with the same root cause (an unbacked mint whose size is unbounded) and the SAME mitigation (bound emission at src/Antimatter.sol:179 / account for the liability). FAITH-002's own text instructs 'Deduplicate against econ-scanner's finding on the same mint at :236 - econ owns the impact sizing'. Its distinct contribution is a QUALIFIER, not a separate remediation: it records that the behaviour is INTENDED, not accidental (Law-1 overriding Law-2 on a faithfully-implemented but unsafe intent). A qualifier with no separate fix does not earn a second submission - it is preserved as `specStatus` inside this entry, and the entry is dual-channelled to spec-conformance so the faithfulness report still carries it. CONTRAST: FAITH-001 is NOT merged here (see DEDUP-015) because 'the written justification is false' has a different root cause (documentation defect), a different remediation (correct the NatSpec), and lands on a different reader (integrators), and because collapsing it would let the doc defect vanish if the econ finding is ever triaged as accepted-by-design.
additionalContext.specStatus: FAITHFUL-BUT-UNSAFE. Law-1 override on Law-2: the declared intent ('this contract mints the phUSD for the antimatter half', :188-189; CLAUDE.md 'antimatter's entire value to a holder is that it annihilates into phUSD worth twice its quantity') is implemented exactly. The intent itself is the hazard. Filed as a spec-level rather than implementation-level security finding.
additionalContext.rootCause: Antimatter.mint (:179) has no cap, schedule, or tie to yield or collateral; :236 mints exactly `amount` phUSD against nothing but the burn of a token that was itself minted for free. No contract anywhere tracks the resulting unbacked supply.
additionalContext.economicImpact: Each outstanding antimatter token is a permanent, exercisable, $1-denominated call on the phUSD collateral pool. Fair value max(0, 2p-1) - which is also why the round trip is not standing free money once antimatter is priced by a market; at p=$1 emitting N antimatter is economically identical to writing an $N cheque against phUSD's backing. phUSD has no redemption path, so this never becomes on-chain insolvency - it becomes peg pressure, and the cash loss lands on whatever protocol-owned liquidity absorbs the annihilator's sell.

steps: Receive N antimatter free as a staking reward (:180)
Acquire N (rescaled) stablecoin at ~$1 - real capital
annihilateFrom(stable,self,self,N): burn N AM, surrender $N stable, receive ~2N phUSD (:236-237)
Sell 2N phUSD into protocol-owned liquidity at price p
Net = 2Np - N GROSS OF THE ANTIMATTER LEG; not a free-money condition - see profitability note
profitableLoop.profitability: CORRECTED 2026-08-18 (review pass): the earlier '100% return per cycle at p=$1.00 / profitable for any p > $0.50' claim double-counted by treating antimatter as free. Antimatter's own fair value is ~max(0, 2p-1), so with market pricing arbitrage drives the round-trip return toward that value and the excess profit toward zero. The finding does NOT rest on an arbitrage yield: the reportable core is that unbacked issuance ships with NO cap, NO budget and NO on-chain liability view. Overstated impact is a pipeline-reject condition, so the inflated framing is withdrawn.
profitableLoop.notAnAtomicAttack: annihilation is one-way; the attacker must actually hold antimatter and actually part with stablecoin. This is why it is Medium, not High.

additionalContext.severityRationale: C4 Medium ('value leak with stated assumptions and external requirements'). NOT High: no assets stolen from a specific victim by a specific attack path, no redemption to fail, nothing bricks, and the multiplier itself is documented intent. NOT Low: the liability is real, permanent, unbounded, lands on parties who never consented, and no on-chain control or even observation of it exists.
additionalContext.escalationTrigger: If antimatter emission is ever wired to a permissionless or high-volume minter via setApprovedMinter (:151), re-weigh as High. See parked PARK-003 - antimatter is not yet wired into phoenix-phase-2-staging, so emission policy is entirely undecided on-chain.
additionalContext.law2Caveat: Intent is UNGRADED, not passed: no storyDir, no [story-NNN] tag on any of the 6 commits (PARK-002). The only intent artefact is in-source NatSpec, which carries no suppression authority and is itself economically inaccurate.
additionalContext.notFiledCheck: The standing Phoenix rule 'externally-derived yield over-payment is opportunity cost, not loss' was CHECKED and found NOT to apply: the finding is dilution of the phUSD collateral base, not over-payment of a reward budget. No 'the pot pays too much' finding is filed.
additionalContext.reweighTrigger: RE-WEIGH AS HIGH if antimatter emission is ever wired to a PERMISSIONLESS or automated/high-volume minter via setApprovedMinter (:151). At that point step 1 of the loop stops being owner-gated and the finding becomes an active, self-serve drain on the phUSD collateral base rather than a policy exposure. Secondary trigger, carried from MR-04: a bug in ANY approved minter contract converts directly into unbacked phUSD, because there is no supply ceiling at :179. Tertiary trigger: if a phUSD redemption path is ever built, the exposure converts from peg pressure into on-chain insolvency and must be re-weighed immediately.
